structure: Caltech Submillimeter Observatory / Leighton 10.4 m telescopes (OVRO and CSO dishes)
construction: 84 hexagonal aluminium-honeycomb panels, about 1.15 m across and about 7 cm thick (NTRS 1977). Panels carry three skins (bottom, centre, top); the top skin is 1.0 mm (0.040 in) sheet aluminium, selected for uniform thickness, etched, epoxy-coated on one side and pulled onto the machined open-cell honeycomb face by about 0.1 atm / 1 psi external (vacuum-bag) pressure. Flat sheet is elastically bent to the panel curvature, which loads the panel (see shape_accuracy).
panel_size: hexagonal, about 1.15 m (Leighton NSF report, NTRS 1976/1977); thickness about 7 cm (NTRS 1977, p.4). Core cell size, adhesive type and brand: null (not found in the pages read).
tooling: No mould. The whole dish (steel tube space frame, panels mounted) sits on an air bearing and rotates under a fixed cutter running on a parabolic cutter track; track set to about 2 um by laser ranging (Phillips) and 3.5 um attained in 1977 (Leighton, item 2 of the error list). The cutter planes the honeycomb to shape; one full cut takes 4-8 h. After the skin is bonded the surface is measured with a linear transducer in the cutter position and contour-mapped (felt-pen colour code). Skins may then be etched (4 % NaOH), ground or lapped; grinding the aluminium skin warped panels by heating, etching worked (NTRS 1977).
cure_method: Epoxy cemented under vacuum-bag / external pressure; cure temperature and schedule: null (the NTRS 1977 report says room-temperature-curing epoxy for the proposed space version). The prototype also tested a pre-strain device that made the cutter remove about 150 um more at panel centre than edge to offset skin rebound.
assembly_and_adjustment: Panels on thin laterally flexible steel rods with differential-screw adjusters (also a Peltier option, Phillips). Panels are removable and re-mountable with reproducibility error 5-15 um (prototype) to 5-10 um (improved), per NTRS 1976 Table 1. Frame is disassembled in sections for shipping; at CSO the reassembled surface was about 40 um, brought to about 20 um by procedures listed in Phillips. Measured on site by shearing-interferometer holography (Serabyn 1991) and later radio holography.

panel_size: US9735466: panels 1.080 in thick; other dimensions null. EP0470271: dimensions null in the pages read.
tooling: EP0470271: open mould cleaned, release agent, gel coat, outer skin, foam placed, inner skin laid up, cured in the mould at 80 C. US9735466: thermoplastic panel held on a vacuum table, edges thermoformed in a heated CNC edge tool then machined on a 5-axis router; no mould.
cure_method: EP0470271: in-mould cure at 80 C. US9735466: heat-and-cool thermoplastic consolidation.
assembly_and_adjustment: EP0470271: bolted joint straps and caps. US9735466: butt edges with pultruded splines bolted about every 4 in, fastener heads covered.

missing: Everything about frame and membrane tolerances.

gaps: No published numeric shape or waviness tolerance for any sandwich radome was found; CPI, Comtech and two patents give sizes, construction and joints only.

Category "other" (boat hulls, wind-turbine blades, domes, launcher fairings) is empty: no opened source gave a shape-accuracy number for a large sandwich shell. Search summaries mentioned a +/-5 mm blade-profile deviation in a patent family and the Ariane 5 fairing (aluminium honeycomb with carbon skins, 5.4 m) but neither was opened or carried a measured tolerance.

Woody 1994 Proc. IEEE (ADS gave a CAPTCHA; no open PDF) and the 1983 Baars SPIE design paper were not opened. IRAM 30 m primary design paper (Fermilab copy) and Greve 1998 A&AS page returned bot challenges or 403 and were not bypassed.

Not covered: Nobeyama 45 m panel numbers (only a title seen), GBT panels (solid aluminium, not sandwich), Effelsberg (a search summary said glued honeycomb panels failed in the inner 60 m; the SHAO page was gone and the claim is unverified), Cassini 4 m HGA (no source with a surface number), Herschel, von Hoerner NRAO reports, CCAT/FYST, SPT, GLT, Planck as-built rms.

Panel dimensions are missing for ALMA AEC, SMT and LMT panels; none of the real precedents is Be-faced or 23 mm core, and the closest analogue (0.6 mm Ni on 20 mm Al honeycomb, ALMA) has only a 8 um panel specification, not a distribution.

No source states a dimple or waviness amplitude at the 0.35 m or 0.1 mm scale for a sandwich panel. The nearest facts are the IRAM panel-scale error correlation length of 0.3-0.5 m (amplitude not given), the CSO 5-10 um panel rms with the 150 um panel rebound correction, and the JAXA finding that tow print-through left several tens of nm.

Cost: only JCMT (GBP 2M refurbish, GBP 5M replace, 2011 estimates), SMT (USD 5-6M estimate, 1987), and the ALMA North American contract (USD 169M for 25 antennas) were found; no cost per square metre of panel.
